headline: G MINING VENTURES TOPS Q3 EPS ESTIMATES, SHARES JUMP 10% — Tocantinzinho Delivers 44,960 oz at $4,000+ Realized Gold
snippet: G Mining Ventures (TSX: GMIN, OTCQX: GMINF) beat Q3 2026 EPS consensus estimates on its full financial results call, sending shares up approximately 10% after hours. Tocantinzinho in Brazil produced 44,960 oz in the quarter — up 22% sequentially — with realized gold prices above $4,000 per ounce underpinning strong margins. The beat is a standout in a week where gold equities broadly underperformed on rate-hike repricing, and positions GMIN as one of the cleaner single-asset gold producer stories on the TSX heading into Q4.

headline: ASX MINING STOCKS LED FRIDAY ROUT — COMEX Gold $3,906, Copper $6.17/lb, Uranium ETF URNM Sinks 5%
snippet: Australian mining stocks led the ASX 200 lower on Friday as NVIDIA-related tech selling, a bond yield spike, and overnight commodity price declines hit the sector simultaneously. COMEX gold fell approximately 2.9% overnight to US$3,906 per ounce while COMEX copper sat near US$6.17 per pound, and the uranium equity ETF URNM dropped 5% in New York — the sharpest single-day move in the uranium sector since late October. The selloff across metals, uranium, and energy underscores how macro risk-off is overriding commodity-specific supply fundamentals for the moment.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES AFTER WORST WEEK SINCE MARCH — China Scramble for Metal With SHFE Stocks at 3-Year Low Provides Footing
snippet: Copper prices staged a modest recovery after recording their worst weekly decline since March 2026, with the AI-equity-linked selloff identified by Goldman Sachs as the primary driver — not weakening Chinese demand. Shanghai Futures Exchange warehouse stocks sat at just 27,642 tonnes, their lowest since December 2023, confirming acute physical tightness that is at odds with the futures-driven selloff. The divergence between weakening paper prices and historically tight physical supply is becoming the defining tension in the copper market heading into year-end.

headline: GOLDMAN: COPPER SELLOFF IS AI-EQUITY CONTAGION, NOT DEMAND — Banks Split Sharply on 2027 Surplus vs. Shortage Outlook
snippet: Goldman Sachs is attributing the recent copper price decline — which sent the metal to a four-month low and produced its worst weekly performance since March — to AI-equity contagion rather than any fundamental demand deterioration, pointing to the record Yangshan import premium and multi-year-low SHFE warehouse stocks as evidence the physical market is tighter than futures pricing implies. The broader analytical picture is fractured: some banks are forecasting a 2027 copper surplus driven by new mine supply, while others see structural underinvestment and accelerating Chinese EV and grid demand pointing to a persistent deficit. For junior copper explorers, the split matters: capex decisions made today will produce into one of two very different macro environments.

headline: GENESIS-VAULT A$5.6B GOLD MEGA-MERGER CLEARS 99.74% SHAREHOLDER VOTE — WA Supreme Court Hearing Set for November 16
snippet: Vault Minerals shareholders voted 99.74% in favour of the scheme of arrangement with Genesis Minerals at a scheme meeting on November 11, clearing the penultimate regulatory hurdle for a deal valued at approximately A$5.6 billion. The Western Australian Supreme Court hearing is scheduled for November 16, with the scheme expected to become effective November 17 and be fully implemented by November 26. Under the terms, Vault shareholders receive 0.7629 new Genesis shares plus A$0.475 cash per share — creating a new multi-million-ounce Australian gold major and the latest in a string of ASX gold consolidations driven by high bullion prices.

headline: CRITICAL METALS CORP SECURES 100% OF TANBREEZ GREENLAND RARE EARTH DEPOSIT — $264.5M Cash Held; Sets 2027 Production Roadmap
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) announced November 11 that it has delivered all 2026 corporate objectives — completing the acquisition of 100% of the Tanbreez alkaline complex in Greenland, one of the largest rare earth deposits in the northern hemisphere, while holding US$264.5 million in cash across the combined entity at approximately $1.36 per share outstanding. The company published a 2027 roadmap focused on advancing Tanbreez toward resource definition and feasibility work. Investors should note the company disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern given zero operating revenue, making cash burn rate and the feasibility timeline key risk factors to monitor.

headline: LOTUS RESOURCES CLEARED FOR FIRST KAYELEKERA URANIUM EXPORT — Orano Facility Accepts Product; Walvis Bay Shipment Targeting November
snippet: Lotus Resources (ASX: LOT) has secured product acceptance from Orano CE's conversion facility in France, the final commercial step needed before its first uranium shipment from Malawi's Kayelekera mine can proceed. The shipment — approximately 145,000 lbs U3O8 in four containers — is booked for export from Walvis Bay, Namibia, with November as the target date, following the completion of an Namibian radiation authority permit in late October. The first export from Malawi's uranium sector in a decade is both a de-risking milestone for Lotus and a data point for investors tracking whether African uranium supply chains are becoming commercially viable at current $90/lb spot prices.

headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS LOG THIRD STRAIGHT GAIN — Critical Metals +3%, USA Rare Earth +3%, MP Materials +2% as Sector Finds Its Footing
snippet: Rare earth equities posted a third consecutive session of gains on November 13, with Critical Metals Corp (CRML) +3%, USA Rare Earth (USAR) +3%, and MP Materials (MP) +2% extending a recovery that began with USAR's 11% jump on November 11 following its post-earnings rebound. The three-day streak comes despite the broader market selloff and suggests selective accumulation is underway in Western critical mineral producers as investors distinguish between companies with near-term production versus pure exploration plays — a bifurcation that is becoming a defining theme in the rare earths sector heading into 2027.

headline: ZACKS HIGHLIGHTS FURY GOLD, GOLD ROYALTY, NEWMONT, B2GOLD AS HEADWIND-RESISTANT PICKS — Sector Still in Bottom 39% of Industries
snippet: Zacks Research named Fury Gold (TSX-V: FURY), Gold Royalty Corp (NYSE American: GROY), Newmont (NYSE: NEM), and B2Gold (TSX: BTO) as stocks well-positioned to navigate current industry headwinds in its latest Mining-Gold industry outlook, even as the Zacks Mining-Gold Industry Rank sits at #149 out of 244 industries — placing the sector in the bottom 39%. The piece frames the pressure as driven by retreating gold prices, rising all-in sustaining costs, and skilled labour shortages — but notes that royalty and streaming structures, strong balance sheets, and high-grade projects insulate the named companies better than the broader sector. For retail investors deciding whether the sector discount is an opportunity or a warning, the analyst note provides a framework for how the most watched names in the coverage universe are navigating the same environment.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM SHORES UP BATTERED LITHIUM DEMAND CASE — BESS Demand +51% in 2025 as Carbonate Prices Crater 14.7% in 30 Days
snippet: Even as Chinese battery-grade lithium carbonate fell 14.7% over the past 30 days to approximately CNY 92,350 per tonne, the structural demand case is being reinforced by a 51% year-over-year surge in battery energy storage system (BESS) demand — part of a broader 29% rise in global lithium-ion battery demand to 1.59 TWh in 2025. The disconnect between spot price weakness and demand volume growth is the core tension lithium investors are navigating: price declines reflect near-term inventory and production overshoots, while the energy storage transition underpins a long-term demand floor that most supply-side forecasts cannot yet match. Junior lithium explorers on the TSX-V and ASX are trading as though the bearish price narrative has fully won, suggesting sector valuations may be pricing in sustained weakness that the BESS data does not support.

headline: GOLD MINERS STAGE PREMARKET REBOUND AFTER INFLATION-DRIVEN SLIDE — Newmont, Barrick, Agnico Eagle All Tick Higher as Selloff Fatigue Sets In
snippet: Gold mining equities — Newmont, Barrick, and Agnico Eagle among them — traded modestly higher in premarket activity on Friday November 13 as bullion staged a partial recovery from its week-long CPI-driven selloff, offering a brief counterpoint to the week's relentless rate-hike repricing pressure. The move was described in market commentary as 'selloff fatigue' rather than a fundamental reversal, with the December Fed rate-hike probability still locked near 70%. For investors considering entry into senior producers, the ongoing compression in gold equity valuations relative to the spot gold price — seniors are trading at multi-year low P/NAV multiples even at $3,900 gold — is the counter-narrative that experienced gold analysts are flagging as the more important signal.
